executiveSummary: GM0935's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 125,563 residents, 44 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, four BRT settlements, three stations and five Dutch logical road-border links are internally coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Maastricht is a dense international Maas city whose consequences depend on Belgian Meuse/Jeker inputs, distinct Maastricht, Itteren, Borgharen, Bosscherveld and Sint Pieter defence/control reaches, urban quays and bridges, the Jeker/Kanjel-Gelei and dry-valley runoff, emergency pumping, A2 tunnel/access state and MUMC+ continuity. The canonical river preset instead holds 3.148932 m from T+24 through T+72, increases affected population-equivalent from 71,525 to 76,320 and ranks Borgharen 30th and Itteren 37th while inland population centres lead. Current Waterinfo has seven point observations and 20 forecasts through T+24 only; none establishes inundation or T+48/T+72. The current Maas2050 programme is reach-specific, Bosscherveld's dam is repaired while bridge/road works continue, and a 1.8 km mobile barrier for Heugem/Randwyck/MUMC+ was announced for mid-2026 with a 3,250 m³/s trigger and a planned autumn exercise, but reviewed evidence does not confirm its incident readiness at audit time. Public registers identify 77 water assets, Enexis/WML/Ziggo territories, one grid-planning sample, 190 antenna sites, 84 education locations, two PM2.5 observations and Maastricht UMC+, but not live connectivity, reserve, acceptance, backup or restoration. Dutch-only transport omits the Liège/Aachen rail and Belgian road/response continuations. Exact hazard, service and recovery claims must be suppressed or labelled synthetic until a selected, time-valid scenario and auditable action/resource state exist; null, empty, stale and horizon-limited inputs remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0935 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0935 as Maastricht in Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Zuid, and report 125,563 residents, density 2,251/km², 22.4% aged 65 or older and 42,398 one-person households. The reference point [5.700910512488931,50.85965951757866] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Forty-four neighbourhoods in seven districts sum to 125,555 residents, eight below the municipal total (-0.006%); published households sum to 73,385 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 28,100. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 125,563 without rewriting observations.
One active BAG place, Maastricht, is contained. Four BRT labels use different feature semantics: Maastricht, Borgharen, Itteren and Mariënwaard. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District-heating and public-charging values are missing in all 44 neighbourhoods; home value is missing three times, cars per household five times, and several benefit/housing variables four or three times. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero. Annual residence omits students/commuters, tourists, event/MECC visitors, patients and cross-border travellers.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Maastricht Water Programme and Climate Adaptation Strategy
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal Water Programme and Climate Adaptation Strategy dated 8 September 2022; policy horizon/actions through 2027/2035; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The strategy treats extreme/long rainfall, urban waterlogging, flooding, heat, drought and biodiversity as related but distinct policy themes and links them to the municipal water chain. It is planning/context evidence, not a live event or operational capacity source.

Maastricht is surrounded by higher ground, so peak rain can produce slope and dry-valley runoff into the city; hard surfaces increase sewer load. This mechanism cannot be represented by municipality-average rain/depth or demographic ranking alone.

The current Water in Balans agreement at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/actueel/nieuws/2025/samen-wateroverlast-overeenkomst-waterschap-limburg/ identifies recurrent water nuisance around Vroenhovenweg and planned buffers plus further investigation of Kleine and Lange Zouw. Agreement/planning state does not prove construction, empty storage, maintenance or event performance.

The strategy supports source-specific pluvial and heat integration using municipal/regional stress-test or programme products. Preserve publication/version, resolution, scenario assumptions, policy evidence class, coverage, uncertainty, NoData and absent blanket licence.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Zuidelijk Maasdal defence programme and announced Heugem-Randwyck mobile barrier
evidenceSources.edition: Maas2050 factsheet version March 2026; mobile-barrier notices published 23–24 February 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The March 2026 authority factsheet identifies five ongoing, distinct reaches: Maastricht 7.0 km, Itteren 3.5 km, Borgharen 3.4 km, Bosscherveld 2.6 km and Sint Pieter 0.9 km. Reinforcement programming is neither current failure nor a municipality-wide safety guarantee.

Waterschap, municipality and MUMC+ announced a 1.8 km mobile barrier on the existing Hoge Weerd/Limburglaan dike for Heugem, Randwyck, MUMC+ and the A2-tunnel area. The stated operational concept starts setup when 3,250 m³/s is forecast at Sint Pieter, takes about four hours and requires sixty people.

The February notice said the barrier would be available mid-2026 and intended to raise the stated protection discharge from about 3,500 to at least 4,000 m³/s, with an exercise planned for autumn 2026. No reviewed follow-up confirms delivered inventory, trained/available sixty-person team, route access, decision authority, exercise completion or current readiness at audit time.

Trigger, setup time, people, alignment and capacity are official design/planning values, not an automatic action or event-time performance. Retain source date and planning/readiness-unknown status until the responsible authorities confirm commissioning and activation.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped Maastricht water observations/forecasts and Maas control/works context
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts retrieved 3 September 2026 04:29Z; current RWS asset/project pages inspected 3 September; Waterinfo CC0, RWS page-level blanket reuse licence not established
supports: Seven observations at 17:30Z on 2 September cover water level and/or discharge at Sint Pieter Noord, Borgharen Dorp, Borgharen Julianakanaal and Smeermaas Zuid-Willemsvaart. Six are publisher-classed normal and Borgharen discharge is classed reduced; these fresh point records are not inundation, defence performance or municipality-wide safety.

Twenty forecast records cover T+1/+6/+12/+24 only: discharge at Sint Pieter/Borgharen and levels at Sint Pieter/Borgharen Maas/Borgharen Julianakanaal. T+24 records are publisher-classed reduced, including a scoped zero discharge forecast at Borgharen; no local T+48/T+72 forecast exists, and station zero is not no river or no risk.

RWS explains at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/waterbeheer/bescherming-tegen-het-water/hoogwater/hoogwaterkaart that high Maas discharge causes stuw Borgharen to open and Keersluis Limmel to close around the stated threshold, interrupting Julianakanaal navigation. This is a conditional control mechanism, not current closure or verified timing.

The current Bosscherveld page at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/projectenoverzicht/maas-herstel-overlaatdam-en-brug-bij-bosscherveld says the new overlaatdam is complete while Overlaatbrug/Stuwweg/Bosscherweg work continues toward end-2026; earlier authority notices call the temporary bridge operational. Project/temporary access context is not live throughput or all-mode availability.

The Bovenmaas definition at https://etl.rijkswaterstaat.nl/rws_legger/ZN/01%20Maas/01_sys_Maas_v1.pdf extends from the Eijsden border to Borgharen and includes a Belgian section. Belgian Meuse/Albert Canal operations are material upstream boundary conditions and absent from a Dutch municipality scalar.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Crisisplan, draft high-water plan, care warning process and first-72-hour guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2024–2027; high-water plan 2026–2029 consultation closed 26 August 2026 but definitive adoption not confirmed; current guidance inspected 3 September; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The current crisis plan includes flexible escalation, prolonged-crisis working and international cooperation. The renewed high-water plan consultation distinguishes regional-system high water, Maas high water and defence-failure/polder effects and adds an Impact Analysis Team, but its definitive adoption was not confirmed at audit time.

GHOR says its care-partner alert/information process now alerts the care network as standard from GRIP 2, a lesson from 2021. This is a process/trigger, not proof that a specific alert was issued or that every care provider received, acknowledged or acted on it.

The 2024 Bosscherveld case required precautionary evacuation of nearby houseboats, GRIP 3, Rijkswaterstaat/Defence response and temporary dam construction over several days. Historical action/resource evidence is useful for workflow tests but is not a reusable current action or performance guarantee.

Current https://app.zuidlimburgveilig.nl/veiligheidsthemas/blijf-72-uur-veilig guidance recommends three days of water/food, medication and communication/lighting preparations plus household plans. Guidance and app/offline availability do not measure stocks, battery, warning reach or universal self-reliance.

evidenceSources.publisher: EMRIC / ProRail / Arriva / Belgian transport authorities
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Euregio response/care and Liège-Maastricht-Heerlen-Aachen transport dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: Current EMRIC pages inspected 3 September 2026; Arriva Drielandentrein service launched 30 June 2024; current 2026 ProRail/Belgian reference services
supports: EMRIC coordinates cross-border fire, technical assistance, emergency care, disaster response and crisis management. It reports roughly 900 cross-border ambulance deployments per year and regional agreements for hospital distribution; agreements/capabilities are not incident-time acceptance, vehicle assignment or completed aid.

Arriva states the Drielandentrein connects Liège, Maastricht, Heerlen and Aachen. ProRail and Belgian operators publish scheduled/reference data, but the generated network terminates at Dutch municipality boundaries and does not represent the Belgian A2/E25/rail continuation or international operational handoffs.

Maastricht's A2, A79, N278, N590, three stations and 203 GTFS stop areas are valid geometry/schedule context. They do not establish current service, bridge/tunnel capacity, border passage, emergency priority, freight/supply throughput or T+72 operation.

Cross-border sources have separate identifiers, editions, cadences and licences: Dutch NWB/ProRail are CC0, while Belgian/GTFS terms vary by publisher. Preserve country, authority, mode, direction, validity and licence; geometry and timetable never become live capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, provider territories, grid planning, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified; exact NBNL/RDI licences not established in consumed metadata
supports: The HWH clip contains 77 realized records: twelve sewer pumps, three wastewater-treatment works (Bosscherveld, Limmel, Heugem), ten surface-water pumps and 52 weirs. Seventy-two capacity values are null; five emergency-pumping values at Borgharen/Itteren have no displayed comparable unit/connectivity in the consumed schema.

Named emergency-pumping points at Borgharen and Itteren support locally distinct seepage/overflow/control workflows, but point/function/realized labels do not establish readiness, fuel/power, crew, connected catchment, compatible capacity or current activation.

A centre-point territory lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, WML water and Ziggo media, all last-updated 7 September 2025; drainage is empty. One Wittevrouwenveld/Enexis planning sample includes demand/injection queues and projects from 2028, but it is not live load, outage, spare capacity or municipal topology.

RDI returns 190 antenna sites and DUO 84 education locations. Locations do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, emergency communication, shelter designation, occupancy, staff or supplies; unknown licence/cadence remains explicit rather than inferred.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Maastricht UMC+ acute-care registration and timestamped local PM2.5 context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; RIVM air observations retrieved 2 September 2026; current MUMC+ pages inspected 3 September
supports: RIVM identifies Maastricht UMC+ inside GM0935 with 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric functions, 24 reported treatment rooms and 23,000 reported 2025 visits. Facility role and annual values do not establish current acceptance, occupancy, staffing, utilities, oxygen, medicines, backup endurance or surge capacity.

MUMC+ is a regional/cross-border high-complexity dependency and lies within the Heugem-Randwyck mobile-barrier concept. Planned protection does not establish hospital continuity or barrier readiness; hospital service state must remain separate.

Two local air stations observed PM2.5 of 5 and 4 µg/m³ at 17:00Z on 2 September. These are timestamped point observations, not a municipal surface, smoke forecast, health-effect estimate or T+72 all-clear.

No reviewed public source supplies current hospital acceptance/diversion, patient/bed state, access-route status, critical utilities, generator/fuel endurance, blood/oxygen/medicine stocks or restoration. Use authorized aggregates only.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services for GM0935.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed the complete deterministic contract: one test file and two tests in 30.42 seconds.
A separate diagnostic enumerated all preset/checkpoint service outputs and detailed neighbourhood ranks; its final focused run passed one test in 14.44 seconds.
Scenario execution coverage is verified; this does not establish local physical or operational calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, reconciliation, determinism, service arithmetic and cumulative burden invariants hold.
notes: Availability values remain in [0,1], UI/sim-core preset factories agree, repeated runs are exact, demand/delivery reconcile and event-attributable person-hours are monotonic.
At T+24 severity spans 0 for earthquake to 0.983914 for river; bounded arithmetic and six-decimal output are not evidence of observed precision.
Synthetic outputs must remain clearly separate from timestamped observations, forecasts, official scenarios, planning values and authorized action state.

spatialPlausibility.summary: River/pluvial allocation conflicts with known Maas-side and runoff mechanisms, while several unrelated hazards reuse a population-led order.
notes: River T+24 reports 3.148932 m, severity 0.983914 and 71,525 affected without a selected hydrograph/datum, Belgian boundary/control, defence/barrier/pump state, connected inundation, arrival or recession.

Heer, Scharn, Daalhof and Amby lead river affected counts. Borgharen ranks 30th with 994 of 1,705 and Itteren 37th with 513 of 920, despite official distinct Maas defence/emergency-pumping context; Heugem ranks 12th and Randwyck 15th despite the named MUMC+/A2 mobile-barrier pathway.
Pluvial T+24 reports 0.453439 m and 23,706 affected without rain, terrain/dry valleys, soil/groundwater, sewers, Jeker/Kanjel/Gelei/Zouw catchments, 77 assets or Maas boundary state.

Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and compound are all dominated by the same population-led sequence. Wildfire has zero direct fire/affected and 0.145952 smoke at T+24, describing preset placement rather than a local all-clear.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service balances calculate, but Maastricht's water, utility, cross-border mobility, care and supply topology/state are unavailable.
notes: River T+24 availability is power 0.422137, water 0.439316, drainage 0.227948, gas 0.673940, telecom 0.396541, mobility 0.466689, facilities 0.543379 and supply 0.460434; no operator validates these exact values.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.323869, water 0.392528, drainage 0.265907, gas 0.572434, telecom 0.202122, mobility 0.612206, facilities 0.335836 and supply 0.461153; these are aggregate synthetic indices.

HWH points, provider territories, one NBNL planning sample, antennas, stops/stations, MUMC+ and EMRIC context do not supply live connectivity, flow/load/quality, control, backup, crews, acceptance, stock, cross-border assignment or restoration.
NWB links may inform road Mobility and explicitly assumed road-logistics Supply only; they must not become power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or care topology.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but missing hydraulic, barrier, pump, border, access, lifeline and authority-action dimensions do not gate displayed consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions, service-stage deltas and weighted service-loss contributions reconcile, and public observations/planning/context layers remain non-causal.

No selected source event supplies Belgian/Sint Pieter hydrograph, water datum, defence/barrier/control state, local footprint, fire ignition/perimeter, cyber target, operator outage, hospital acceptance or confirmed authority action.

Waterinfo is timestamped and quality-scoped but stops at T+24; design trigger/setup values and cross-border agreements require separate governed adapters and cannot silently become completed actions or performance.
Unsupported exact depth, affected, availability and burden values must be marked synthetic screening/Unknown locally and expose missing dimensions on maps, briefs and exports.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and recovering impacts through T+72 are deterministic but unsupported by hydraulics, operators, access/care state or confirmed actions.
notes: River holds severity 0.983914 and depth 3.148932 from T+24 through T+72 while affected rises 71,525 to 76,320 and burden reaches 4,641,206.85; every service except facilities is exactly unchanged and facilities falls 0.543379 to 0.349773 without hydraulic or operational cause.

Compound severity falls 0.933287 to 0.520754 from T+24 to T+72 while depth stays 0.468903, affected rises 83,137 to 83,732 and burden reaches 4,987,827.33; all services worsen slightly without action/repair evidence.

Storm/pluvial/winter direct effects clear to zero by T+72 while burdens persist; coastal has zero direct affected but degraded services. None is validated by recession, dewatering, inspection, barrier removal, bridge/tunnel reopening, care continuity, repair or resupply evidence.

Only confirmed validity-aligned IAT/GRIP, defence/barrier/pump/control, access, care, utility, cross-border aid, logistics and welfare actions may alter recovery. Seventy-two hours is preparedness scope, not a restoration promise.

findings.summary: Generated identity, settlements, regional membership and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0935, Maastricht, Limburg, Limburg-Zuid, the contained centre, one BAG place and annual population agree; 44 neighbourhoods total only eight fewer residents than the municipal control and reconcile exactly.
findings.action: Retain source edition/retrieval time, full-resolution geometry access, published-versus-allocated values, null semantics and evidence class on refresh.

findings.summary: Null variables, empty feeds and missing forecast/operational fields remain Unknown/NoData.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging are null in all 44 rows, 72/77 HWH capacity values are null, provider drainage and bounded NDW are empty, no local KNMI station/seismic event exists, Waterinfo stops at T+24, and utility/care operational states are absent.
findings.action: Preserve publisher, version, retrieval/issue/valid time, licence or unknown licence, spatial/temporal coverage, evidence class, NoData mask and reason. Never coerce absence or scoped station zero to no event, normal, dry, safe, open or available.

findings.summary: The river preset assigns unsupported 3.148932 m depth without the cross-border Maas, defence/control and connected-footprint state that governs Maastricht.
findings.evidence: River holds 3.148932 m from T+24 through T+72 and reports 71,525 then 76,320 affected, but names no Belgian/Sint Pieter hydrograph, datum, reach, barrier/pump/control state, breach/overtopping/seepage, connected cell, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth, affected counts, percentages and hotspots until an authority-governed scenario binds upstream boundary/station/datum, defence/control state, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData. Retain general high-water preparedness and labelled official point context.

findings.summary: Point observations/forecasts through T+24 cannot validate or extend the simulated T+72 flood state.
findings.evidence: Seven observations and 20 forecasts distinguish level/discharge, station, unit/datum, quality and valid time. Forecasts end at T+24; a Borgharen discharge forecast of zero is station/parameter-specific and no local T+48/T+72 value or inundation/defence state exists.
findings.action: Keep observation, forecast, official scenario and synthetic output separate. Display issue/valid/retrieval time, station, parameter, unit/datum and quality; expire missing horizons to NoData and never hold/interpolate or translate point normal/reduced/zero into municipality safety.

findings.summary: Reach programmes and the announced Heugem-Randwyck mobile barrier lack incident-valid readiness/action state.
findings.evidence: Five Maas2050 reaches are ongoing. The mobile barrier has a stated 3,250 m³/s setup trigger, four-hour setup and sixty-person requirement, but the February source only planned mid-2026 availability and an autumn exercise; no reviewed follow-up confirms commissioning, team/resource availability or deployment.
findings.action: Retain reach/programme and barrier design as non-causal planning context. Require authority, forecast trigger, inventory/readiness, trained/assigned resources, access, command decision, started/completed/verified timestamps and expiry before the barrier changes protection or recovery; never infer planned equals available/deployed.

findings.summary: Pluvial output omits Maastricht's slope/dry-valley, urban sewer, stream and receiving-Maas mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.453439 m and 23,706 affected without rainfall hyetograph, AHN surface/depressions, hard surface, soil/groundwater, sewer state, Jeker/Kanjel/Gelei/Kleine-Lange Zouw catchments, 77 controls or receiving-Maas level.
findings.action: Integrate governed municipal/water-board stress or hydraulic surfaces with KNMI rain, AHN/BGT/BRO/land cover, sewer-included flag, soil/saturation, catchments, controls and Maas boundary. Preserve resolution, CRS, version/licence, validity, uncertainty and NoData; otherwise suppress exact depth/exposure.

findings.summary: Population-led allocation under-ranks explicit Maas-side/control areas and is reused across unrelated hazards.
findings.evidence: River ranks Borgharen 30th, Itteren 37th, Heugem 12th and Randwyck 15th while inland population centres lead, despite their named defence, emergency-pump and mobile-barrier pathways. Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and compound share the same leading population pattern.
findings.action: Remove shared demographic ranking from hotspot claims. Use separate source geometry for Maas/streams/pluvial, paved/tree-canopy heat, wind/ice, cyber targets and fire/smoke; render local distribution Unknown until supported and regression-test Borgharen/Itteren/Heugem/Randwyck/Bosscherveld pathways.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, wildfire/smoke, earthquake, coastal and cyber presets remain bounded but locally uncalibrated exercises.

Two PM2.5 points are observations, not smoke forecasts; no ignition, ground-motion event, direct coastal pathway or named cyber event/target is selected, while zero-direct presets still create burden.
